comments: DISSERTATION PBPK28 PARITY REFERENCE — DEGENERATE (V_v→0, PS→∞)
Companion to website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs and the parity gate at
scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh (Case 2: asymptotic reduction
of PBPK28 → PBPK14 well-stirred).
Degenerate configuration:
vasc_frac_at(i) = 1e-3 ∀ organs (vs 0.019–0.282 in the literature ref)
ps_at(i)        = lit_PS_i × 1e4   (drives PS-coupling instantaneous)
At these parameters CN's A-stability is essential — explicit RK4 in the
slow operator would require dt ~ 1e-7 h for kidney/lung; CN integrates
stably at dt = 0.001 h.
CORRECTED asymptotic claim (G-α-β math correction):
PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞) does NOT reduce to PBPK14 well-stirred. It
reduces to a *1-state quasi-steady-state (QSS) model*:
V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release,
V_eff = V_b + Σ V_i · Kp_i
C_v_i = C_b instantly; C_t_i = Kp_i · C_b instantly.
PBPK14 well-stirred sits BETWEEN PBPK28-lit (finite PS, finite V_v) and
PBPK28-degenerate (V_v→0, PS→∞). The three models form a hierarchy in
model-form complexity; PBPK14 is the *intermediate* approximation where
tissue redistributes instantly *within* an organ but blood-to-tissue
transport remains rate-limited by Q. PBPK28-degenerate additionally
assumes blood-to-tissue transport is also instantaneous.
This file remains useful as: (a) the target trajectory for the
fully-coupled CN A-stability proof at extreme stiffness, and (b) the
numerical demonstration that PBPK28-degenerate matches the 1-state QSS
limit (asymptotic verification of the model-reduction theorem).
Quantitative match against the 1-state QSS limit at literature
parameters provides the Type B model-form uncertainty contribution per
JCGM 100:2008 §4.3 (the G-α-γ follow-up will emit benchmarks/pbpk/
model_form_uc.csv from these comparisons).
Model: permeability-limited PBPK, 14 organs × {vascular, interstitial}.
V_v,i · dC_v,i/dt = Q_i·(C_blood - C_v,i) - PS_i·(C_v,i - C_t,i/Kp_i)
V_t,i · dC_t,i/dt = PS_i·(C_v,i - C_t,i/Kp_i)
V_b   · dC_b/dt   = sum_i Q_i·(C_v,i - C_b) - cl_hep·C_b
Integrator: fully-coupled Crank-Nicolson on the 27-state PBPK28 system —
no operator splitting. PS coupling and Q transport integrated implicitly in
one CN step via per-organ Schur-complement elimination + scalar reduction
for C_blood. A-stable, 2nd-order, no splitting-induced bias.
Compartment indexing matches website/src/components/dissertation/compartments.ts:
0=blood 1=liver 2=kidney 3=brain 4=heart 5=lung 6=muscle 7=adipose
8=gut   9=skin  10=bone   11=spleen 12=pancreas 13=other
Bolus 0.05 mg into blood (C_blood(0) = 0.01 mg/L). cl_hep = 12.4 L/h. Stent off.
Twelve log-spaced sample times. Emits PARITY|t / PARITY|i / PARITY|cv / PARITY|ct
/ PARITY|cavg records — the gate joins on (t, i) and compares against the
Node runner's identical output.

The ZD-geometry report (SEDENION_ZERO_DIVISOR_GEOMETRY_REPORT.md) left this OPEN: it found the
zero-divisor side has no factor 11, and conjectured "the 11 in 1848 = 11*168 belongs to the
associator side". This test EXECUTES the associator side and confirms it exactly.
For sedenion basis units e_i, e_j, e_k the associator [e_i,e_j,e_k] = (e_i e_j)e_k - e_i(e_j e_k)
is a single component e_(i^j^k) with integer coefficient
A(i,j,k) = sigma(i,j)*sigma(i^j,k) - sigma(j,k)*sigma(i,j^k)   in {-2, 0, +2}.
A triple is non-associative iff A != 0. Over the 15*14*13 = 2730 ORDERED distinct triples of
imaginary units {1..15}:
* exactly 1848 are non-associative, and 1848 = 11 * 168 = 11 * |PSL(2,7)|;
* by output grade s = i^j^k: each of the 14 grades s != 8 carries exactly 120, and the doubling
grade s = 8 carries 168 (= the octonion associator count). So 1848 = 14*120 + 168 = 10*168 + 168,
i.e. the "11" splits as 11 = 10 + 1 (the doubling grade contributes the +1*168);
* the octonion sub-tower {1..7} contributes exactly 168 ordered non-associative triples.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs
scripts/research/sedenion_associator_1848_oracle.py by scripts/ci/sedenion_associator_1848_gate.sh

comments: A refinement must hold at the RETURN, not only at a binding.
This is the Madaros half of a measured engine divergence. On main@88c2ab8ee8
the *mut checker spine calls checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace from
exactly two places (check.sio:9627, 9687), both in the let/var handlers, and
check/compat.sio never looks at refinement_id. So under Madaros a refinement
is enforced where a value is BOUND and nowhere else:
$ artifacts/madaros --check tests/compile-fail/refinement_f64_return_violation.sio
check: OK
lean_single rejects the same file. tests/known_failures/
hardened_diagnostics_full_suite.txt records the split in its own words
(2026-08-23): "default Madaros still answers `check: OK` on that file, so the
refinement is unenforced there; that is a compiler defect, not a manifest
one." This test is that defect, pinned for the integer case.
SCOPE. checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace only fires when
last_literal_kind is 1 (int) or 2 (float), so this pins the LITERAL return.
The propagated case is a separate, still-open hole:
fn lift(x: i64) -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { x }        // still accepted
fn f() -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { let b = 0 - 7  return b }  // still accepted
Those need dataflow the checker does not have here; main's own
tests/compile-fail/refinement_return_var.sio pins that case for lean_single
and is untouched by this test. Closing the literal case is what the
known-failures manifest asks for, and is where the fix stops.
The refinement is written INLINE, not through a `type` alias. A named alias
takes a different path on the *mut spine (checker_lower_named_type_mut does
not consult the refinement table) and fails with E008 "expected Fp, found
i64" long before the refinement is consulted -- a separate, unfixed defect
that this test deliberately does not depend on.
